definitions.explanation: A Japanese dish of fresh raw fish or meat sliced into thin pieces, served with soy sauce and wasabi.

examples.japanese: {刺身|さしみ}{盛|も}り{合|あ}わせを{注文|ちゅうもん}した。
examples.english: I ordered an assorted sashimi platter.

examples.japanese: この{刺身|さしみ}はとても{新鮮|しんせん}だ。
{刺身|さしみ}は{醤油|しょうゆ}と{山葵|わさび}で{食|た}べる。
examples.english: Sashimi is eaten with soy sauce and wasabi.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: {刺|さ}し (to pierce) + {身|み} (flesh/meat)

COMMON TYPES:
・{鮪|まぐろ} (tuna)
・{鮭|さけ}/{サーモン|さーもん} (salmon)
・{鯛|たい} (sea bream)
・{鰹|かつお} (bonito)
・{烏賊|いか} (squid)

SERVING STYLE:
・{刺身|さしみ}{盛|も}り{合|あ}わせ (assorted sashimi platter)
・{舟盛|ふなも}り (sashimi served on a boat-shaped plate)
・{姿造|すがたづく}り (whole fish sashimi presentation)

CONTRAST WITH SUSHI: Sashimi is just the raw fish; sushi includes vinegared rice.
